# Community Rule Column 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QS (Cave 1), Col. 11 | **Condition:** complete

---

**11:1** I will sing with understanding, and every melody I make will honor God; my lyre and harp will serve His sacred purpose,

**11:2** and the song on my lips I will lift up to His perfect standard.

**11:3** When day and night arrive, I will enter God's covenant; when evening departs and morning comes, I will recite His laws.

**11:4** Within them I will mark my boundaries and never turn back.

**11:5** As for me, God alone holds my case; in His hand rests the wholeness of my path and the integrity of my heart;

**11:6** and through His righteousness He will wipe away my sin.

**11:7** For He has opened my eyes from the wellspring of His wisdom, and I have glimpsed His wondrous works;

**11:8** the light within my heart has seen the mystery of what is to come.

**11:9** The Eternal One is the strength beneath my right hand; my steps rest upon an unshakable rock;

**11:10** nothing can make them falter.

**11:11** For God's truth — that is the bedrock beneath my feet; His power upholds my right hand,

**11:12** and from the wellspring of His righteousness flows my vindication.

**11:13** A light burns in my heart from His astonishing secrets; my eyes have looked upon what lasts forever:

**11:14** wisdom concealed from mortals, insight and deep understanding

**11:15** kept hidden from the human race; a wellspring of right living and a deep reserve of power

**11:16** together with a fountain of splendor — all hidden from those bound to the flesh.

**11:17** But to those God has chosen, He has granted these things as an everlasting gift; He has given them a share

**11:18** among the holy ones; with the angels of heaven He has joined their fellowship

**11:19** into a council of true community and a foundation built on holiness — an eternal planting through all ages to come.

**11:20** But as for me, I belong to sinful humanity, to the company of corrupt flesh; my failings, my rebellions, my sins,

**11:21** along with the depravity of my heart — all these belong to the realm of decay and to those who stumble in the dark.

**11:22** For no one charts their own course; no mortal directs their own steps. Judgment belongs to God alone, and from His hand comes the wholeness of every path.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The closing hymn of 1QS is among the most theologically profound passages in the Dead Sea Scrolls. The speaker moves from ecstatic praise to a staggering confession of human nothingness before God. The "mystery of what is to come" (raz nihyeh) is a uniquely Qumran concept — the idea that God has revealed the secret pattern of future history to the elect. The final lines (11:20-22) are breathtaking in their humility: the worshiper who has just described seeing eternal mysteries now declares himself nothing more than worms and dust. This radical contrast between divine gift and human unworthiness defines Qumran spirituality.*
